a_records.quote: Suppose the baseline survival function is F_bar(x) = 1/x, x >= 1. It can be shown that F_bar_alpha(alpha x) is increasing and log-convex in alpha for alpha >= x >= 1. Take the Ali-Mikhail-Haq copula generator phi(u) = u^{1-delta}/(e^u - delta) ... for (delta = 0.8), delta in (0,1), the function u psi'(1-u) is decreasing in u. For p = (0.72, 0.18, 0.02), alpha = (37, 24, 5) and lambda = (7, 4, 2) we have alpha <=^w lambda. The survival functions of X^p_{3:3} and Y^p_{3:3} are shown in Figure 1(a), which yields the stochastic ordering X^p_{3:3} <=st Y^p_{3:3}.
a_records.family: SAH marginals with Pareto-type baseline F_bar(x) = 1/x; AMH copula delta = 0.8; random shocks

b_records.quote: Example 1. Let the baseline survival function be F_bar(x) = 1/x, x >= 1; F_bar_alpha(x/alpha) is increasing and log-convex in alpha for alpha >= x >= 1. Consider the Ali-Mikhail-Haq copula generator phi(u) = u^{1-delta}/(e^u - delta) with psi(u) = log((1-delta+delta u)/u) for delta in [-1,1], u in (0,1]; for delta = 0.8, u psi'(1-u) is decreasing in u. For p = (0.72, 0.18, 0.02), alpha = (37, 24, 5) and lambda = (7, 4, 2) we have alpha <=_w lambda. The survival functions of X_{3:3}^p and Y_{3:3}^p shown in Fig. 1(a) yield X_{3:3}^p <=st Y_{3:3}^p.
b_records.family: Pareto-type baseline F_bar(x) = 1/x; AMH copula delta = 0.8; Bernoulli shocks

a_records.quote: Consider two parallel systems of dependent and heterogeneous components with baseline survival function F_bar(x) = 1/x, x >= 1. It can be shown that the properties of being increasing and log-convex in alpha do NOT hold for F_bar_alpha(alpha x). Also let alpha = (11, 8, 4) in D+, lambda = (9, 6, 2) in D+ and p = (0.92, 0.68, 0.32) in D+, where alpha <=^w lambda. Take the Ali-Mikhail-Haq generators phi_1(u) = u^{0.5}/(e^u - 0.5) and phi_2(u) = 1.6/(e^u + 0.6) such that psi_2 o phi_1 is super-additive (since it is convex), while u psi_2'(1-u) is increasing. By the argument of Example 1, the survival functions of X^p_{3:3} and Y^p_{3:3} are plotted in Figure 2(c), showing X^p_{3:3} not <=st Y^p_{3:3} and Y^p_{3:3} not <=st X^p_{3:3}. Therefore the result of Theorem 3 does not hold.
a_records.family: SAH marginals, baseline F_bar(x) = 1/x; two different AMH-type generators; random shocks

hypotheses.text: F_bar_alpha(alpha x) fails to be increasing and log-convex in alpha

conclusion.direction: no stochastic ordering in either direction (survival functions cross)

b_records.quote: Example 3. Two parallel systems of dependent heterogeneous components with baseline survival F_bar(x) = 1/x, x >= 1; for F_bar_alpha(x/alpha) the increasing property holds but it is not log-convex in alpha. With alpha = (11,8,4) in D+, lambda = (9,6,2) in D+ and p = (0.92,0.68,0.32) in D+, alpha <=_w lambda. AMH generators phi_1(u) = u^{0.5}/(e^u - 0.5) and phi_2(u) = u^{1.6}/(e^u + 0.6): psi_2 o phi_1 is convex hence super-additive and u psi_2'(1-u) is increasing. Fig. 2(c) shows the survival functions of X_{3:3}^p and Y_{3:3}^p cross: X_{3:3}^p not <=st Y_{3:3}^p and Y_{3:3}^p not <=st X_{3:3}^p. Hence Theorem 3's conclusion fails.

a_records.quote: Suppose the baseline survival function is F_bar(x) = e^{-x}, x > 0. The function F_bar_alpha(alpha x) is increasing and convex in alpha. Also take the generator phi(u) = (1 + delta u)^{1/delta} for delta = 0.2, which is convex (equivalently 1 - phi is log-concave) but phi(1-phi)/phi' is decreasing but NOT convex. For alpha = (3,4,5,6) and lambda = (2,4,5,7) and p = (0.2,0.25,0.45,0.8), clearly alpha <=^m lambda holds. Figure 3(a) shows the failure of Theorem 4.

a_records.quote: Consider two series systems consisting of dependent components with baseline survival function F_bar(x) = e^{-x}, x >= 0. Clearly log F_bar_alpha(alpha x) = -alpha^{-4} x^5. It can be easily shown that the second derivative of this function is negative and its first derivative is non-positive. Therefore the condition that F_bar_alpha(alpha x) is increasing and log-concave in alpha holds. Also let alpha = (11,8,4) in D+, lambda = (9,6,2) in D+ and p = (0.92,0.18,0.02) in D+, such that alpha <=^w lambda. The Archimedean generator phi(u) = 2/(1+e^u) is log-concave ... In Figure 3(b) the distribution functions of X^p_{1:3} and Y^p_{1:3} are plotted, showing the graph of F_{X^p_{1:3}} lies above that of F_{Y^p_{1:3}}. Therefore the validity of Theorem 8 is confirmed.
a_records.family: SAH marginals; generator phi(u) = 2/(1+e^u); random shocks

hypotheses.text: alpha <=^w lambda; phi log-concave; F_bar_alpha(alpha x) increasing log-concave in alpha

conclusion.direction: X^p_{1:3} <=_st Y^p_{1:3} (cdf of X above cdf of Y, Figure 3(b))

b_records.quote: Example 5. Two series systems of dependent components with baseline survival F_bar(x) = e^{-x^5}, x >= 0; log F_bar_alpha(x/alpha) = -alpha^{-4} x^5 whose first derivative in alpha is non-negative and second derivative non-positive, so F_bar_alpha(x/alpha) is increasing and log-concave in alpha. With alpha = (11,8,4) in D+, lambda = (9,6,2) in D+ and p = (0.92,0.18,0.02) in D+, alpha <=_w lambda. The generator phi(u) = 2/(1+e^u) is log-concave. Fig. 3(b) shows the distribution function of X_{1:3}^p lies above that of Y_{1:3}^p, confirming Theorem 8.

records.quote: Theorem 5. Let X^p and Y^p be dependent heterogeneous random vectors with X_i ~ SAH(alpha_i, theta_i) and Y_i ~ SAH(alpha_i, eta_i) with a common Archimedean copula generator phi, and I_{pi} independent Bernoulli variables. If F_bar_alpha(x/alpha) is increasing in alpha and (alpha,p) in A_n, (theta,p) in B_n, (alpha,theta) in B_n, then: (a) if phi is log-convex, theta <=_w eta => X_{1:n}^p <=st Y_{1:n}^p; (b) if phi is log-concave, theta <=_w eta => Y_{1:n}^p <=st X_{1:n}^p.

records.quote: A series air-pollution monitoring system of three sensors ... baseline lifetime Weibull with F_bar(x) = e^{-(lambda x)^beta}, lambda = 0.001, beta = 0.7. alpha = (1,1,1), theta = (0.0008, 0.0010, 0.0012) and eta = (0.0005, 0.0010, 0.0015) such that theta <=^w eta. AMH copula with generator phi(u) = e^{1-\delta u} ... wait, printed as phi(u) = e^{1-\delta u}/... with delta = 0.8 (phi log-convex). Shock survival probability p = (0.92,0.92,0.92). Table 1 empirical distribution functions: t = 100: 0.1183 vs 0.1251; t = 300: 0.4679 vs 0.4823; t = 500: 0.7258 vs 0.7405; t = 700: 0.8801 vs 0.8912 ... Hence F_X(t) >= F_Y(t) for all t, equivalently X <=st Y. This result fully confirms the prediction of Theorem 6(a).

records.quote: Case study: validation of Theorem 6 in a series environmental monitoring system. Three series sensors with Weibull baseline F_bar(x) = e^{-(lambda x)^beta}, lambda = 0.001, beta = 0.7; alpha = (1,1,1); additive-hazard vectors theta = (0.0008, 0.0010, 0.0012) and eta = (0.0005, 0.0010, 0.0015) with theta <=_w eta; AMH copula delta = 0.8 (phi log-convex); p = (0.92, 0.92, 0.92). Table 1 gives empirical CDFs: at t = 100, 300, 500, 700, F_hat_Y(t) = 0.1183, 0.4679, 0.7258, 0.8801 and F_hat_X(t) = 0.1251, 0.4823, 0.7405, 0.8912; F_X(t) >= F_Y(t) for all t, i.e. X <=st Y, confirming Theorem 6(a).
records.family: Weibull baseline (lambda = 0.001, beta = 0.7); AMH copula delta = 0.8; homogeneous shock probability
